extracted.intended_audience: health care providers, covered entities, health plan issuers, legal counsel, and other stakeholders subject to HHS OCR Section 1557 regulations
extracted.subtask_description: Interpretation and implementation guidance for nondiscrimination obligations under Section 1557 of the ACA, including treatment of abortion-related refusals, associational discrimination, and nondiscrimination requirements for patient care decision support tools (including AI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of section 1557 nondiscrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1557 prohibits discrimination on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability in covered health programs or activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to covered health programs or activities that receive Federal financial assistance. OCR reads section 1557 consistently with related statutes (title IX, title VI, the Age Act, section 504) as incorporating the ‘‘ground’’ of discrimination and enforcement mechanisms, but the scope is limited to what Congress specified in section 1557. Discriminatory treatment must be tied to a prohibited ground (e.g., refusing a service to a patient because of their race or disability could violate section 1557).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider refusal to provide abortions does not itself constitute discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered provider's decision not to provide abortions or abortion coverage does not itself constitute discrimination in violation [of] section 1557.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declining to provide, pay for, cover, or refer for abortions is not discrimination under section 1557 when done based on religious or conscience objections, professional or business judgments about services offered, or other nondiscriminatory reasons. However, if a provider who generally offers abortion care refuses service to a particular patient for a prohibited reason (e.g., race or disability), that refusal could violate section 1557.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious freedom and conscience protections and §92.302 procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR will enforce and comply with applicable religious freedom and conscience protections, and the rule includes a procedure whereby recipients may rely on such protections or seek assurance of those protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated protections include section 1303 of the ACA, the Weldon, Church, and Coats-Snowe Amendments, RFRA, and other applicable laws. The final rule adds §92.302 to provide a process for recipients who wish to rely on or seek assurance of these protections. OCR also promulgated a separate final rule codifying safeguards for Federal conscience protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-incorporation of Title IX abortion neutrality and religious-exception provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1557 incorporates certain parts of title IX (the ‘‘ground’’ of discrimination and enforcement mechanisms) but does not incorporate provisions that do not define a ground of discrimination or an enforcement mechanism, including title IX's religious exception and abortion neutrality provision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR's reading gives effect to the statutory text limiting incorporation to specific aspects of the referenced statutes. The abortion neutrality provision is characterized as a rule of construction for title IX, not an enforcement mechanism or definitional ground, and thus is not imported into section 1557 by operation of the statutory language.

rubrics_metrics.name: EMTALA obligations unaffected by this rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this rule changes or otherwise affects any health care provider's obligations with respect to EMTALA, including rights, remedies, procedures, or legal standards available under section 1303(c) of the ACA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR does not enforce EMTALA and directs readers to the EMTALA discussion under §92.3. The final rule does not alter EMTALA's existing obligations and does not change State licensing, health, or safety laws; comments asserting a regulatory ‘‘abortion mandate’’ via EMTALA are outside the scope of this rule. The major questions doctrine is not implicated because the rule does not make such changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associational nondiscrimination (§92.209)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities are prohibited from discriminating against an individual on the basis of the race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability of an individual with whom the individual is known to have a relationship or association.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The provision protects individuals (including children, elders, and caregivers) who associate with people in protected classes (e.g., LGBTQI+, persons with SUD). OCR clarifies §92.209 to prohibit discrimination against both individuals and entities (e.g., a health plan discriminating against an entity because it serves patients with LEP, LGBTQI+ populations, or provides MOUD). Associational discrimination may intersect with other provisions (e.g., §§92.101, 92.206, 92.207, 92.208).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on discrimination via patient care decision support tools (§92.210)
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity must not discriminate against any individual on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability through the use of patient care decision support tools (formerly described as 'clinical algorithms').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR adopted the term 'patient care decision support tool' to cover the range of tools used to guide clinical decision-making. The rule applies to tools used at the individual patient level and tools used in administrative or population-level decision-making when they affect patient care, including prior authorization and medical necessity analyses. Covered entities must identify and mitigate potential discrimination arising from these tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and scope of 'patient care decision support tool' (§92.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Patient care decision support tool’ means any automated or non-automated tool, mechanism, method, technology, or combination thereof used by a covered entity to support clinical decision-making in its health programs or activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition expressly includes automated decision systems and AI, predictive decision support interventions (Predictive DSIs), evidence-based tools that rely on rules/thresholds, and non-automated tools (e.g., flowcharts, clinical guidelines). §92.210 applies to section 1557 covered entity users of such tools; developers may also be subject to ONC requirements for Predictive DSIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of tools and settings covered; administrative uses may be discriminatory
rubrics_metrics.description: Patient care decision support tools include flowcharts, clinical guidelines, complex computer algorithms, decision support interventions, models, and tools used in administrative functions (e.g., budgeting, billing, utilization management, eligibility and enrollment, provider contracting, pricing) that affect access to care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR solicited comment and confirmed that the provision covers tools beyond narrowly 'clinical' algorithms because administrative tools can materially impact individuals' access to care and the quality of services. Coverage includes tools used in skilled nursing facilities, allocation of home and community-based services, Medicaid eligibility systems, and hospital risk-adjustment models that affect treatment protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples and anti‑patterns of discriminatory decision-support tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of discriminatory tools include a Crisis Standards of Care flowchart that screens out individuals with disabilities without individualized assessment, and a race‑adjusted eGFR equation that applies a coefficient resulting in higher thresholds (delaying advanced care) for Black patients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR explains that non- individualized assumptions, thresholds, or unexamined training data can produce discriminatory outcomes. Covered entities must account for how an individual's disability or age could affect assessment factors and provide necessary modifications, and must scrutinize assumptions (e.g., race adjustments) that have discriminatory effects on access to equivalent levels of care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between section 1557 and the Pregnancy Discrimination Act/Title VII
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1557 applies to discrimination in health programs or activities that receive Federal financial assistance; the Pregnancy Discrimination Act (amending Title VII) applies to employment settings and is enforced in that context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR does not enforce the Pregnancy Discrimination Act. Section 1557, title IX, and title VII are read consistently to apply similar protections in their respective contexts, but OCR will provide outreach, trainings, and individualized assistance to clarify the scope and application of section 1557 protections relating to pregnancy and related conditions.
